risks: model ranking does not hold across windows
series is close to noise; fitted weights would overfit
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~11% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (2 points, ~2% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.014), which favours a robust combination.

Try a weighted combination with inverse error to test a different weighting scheme (model ranking unstable, but still try).
The series has unstable ranking and several correlated error groups; a robust estimator like median may outperform trimmed mean.
Try a per-horizon weighting with softmax_neg_error to capture potential horizon‑specific strengths in this highly seasonal, low‑predictability series.
Test a simple mean combination to see if a non-robust estimator can beat trimmed mean given strong seasonality and low predictability.
Test a per‑horizon weighted scheme using the top‑k mean per horizon handle (w4) to see if horizon‑specific averaging improves over global weights.
Test a per‑subset weighted softmax on the top‑5 models (pool4) to see if a smaller robust pool improves over trimmed_mean, given unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combination to capture possible horizon‑specific best models (horizon dependence).
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a data‑driven Bayesian average (dba) might adapt to correlated errors better than trimmed mean.
The series has unstable ranking and several correlated groups; testing a per‑horizon weighted combo on a focused pool may capture horizon‑specific strengths.

The series has unstable ranking and many correlated groups; try a weighted combination on a smaller, more diverse pool (pool4) using inverse_error to see if a focused weighted scheme improves over trimmed mean.
test a simple non‑robust mean on the reduced pool4 to see if a smaller subset improves performance given unstable ranking.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.929. Series context: trend strength 0.9996 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.014); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.59.
